The AM process typically results in higher surface roughness compared to conventional manufacturing.
Surface roughness can lead to significant deviations in aerodynamic characteristics and combustion processes compared to design concepts.
The new integral wall model for LES (iWLES) is implemented as a user-defined function in the ANSYS Fluent software.

The iWLES model can capture changes in flow dynamics due to surface roughness, such as swirler effective area, bulk swirl number, pressure distribution, velocity profiles, and turbulence kinetic energy.
The periodic channel flow simulation showed good agreement between the wall shear stress computed using the iWLES UDF and the no-slip boundary condition.
The flat plate benchmark case simulates a subsonic boundary layer developing over a flat plate with distributed roughness elements.
The iWLES model uses a drag coefficient of 0.1 and a roughness areal density of 1 as parameters for the flat plate case.
